# npm-audit allowlist / exception register — high/critical PROD advisories the
# npm-scan CI gate tolerates, each with a documented reason + compensating
# control + tracked fix. One advisory URL per line (# = comment). This file IS
# the auditable exception record: review it at EVERY dependency bump and delete
# an entry the moment its fix ships. An advisory NOT listed here fails the build.
#
# ===========================================================================
# Angular 18.2 framework advisories (SEC-002 / UI-001) — 10 high-severity.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ROOT CAUSE: all are in @angular/{common,compiler,core} at <= 18.2.14.
# FIX: none exists inside the Angular 18.x line — every advisory's only fix is
#   a SEMVER-MAJOR Angular upgrade (npm audit reports 20.x/22.x). The
#   remediation is therefore the Angular 18 -> latest-LTS upgrade, tracked as
#   backlog item UI-001, ELEVATED TO P1 by these advisories.
# RISK ACCEPTANCE (interim, re-assessed each release) with compensating controls:
#   * XSS class (SVG script/animation, i18n attribute bindings, DOM clobbering):
#     the app serves a strict CSP (script-src 'self', no inline/eval — verified
#     on every response by SecurityHardeningTests), which forecloses the script-
#     injection vector these sanitization bypasses rely on.
#   * DoS/OOM (Date/Number pipes): bounded by the API rate limiter (SEC-013) and
#     the reverse proxy; the SPA is a thin client over a paginated API.
#   * XSRF token leakage / HTTP cache info-leak / weak cache-key hashing: the
#     deployment is SAME-ORIGIN with no CORS (ADR-0007) and TLS-only (ADR-0002);
#     the SPA does not rely on Angular's protocol-relative XSRF or shared HTTP
#     caching across origins. Residual risk accepted pending the upgrade.
#
